claims.rationale: MBD2 was identified as a core component of a methyl-CpG-binding repressor complex in primary erythroid cells and demonstrated to functionally mediate developmental globin gene silencing in humans.

refusals.reason: The available pre-cutoff evidence characterizes ASH1L as an active gene histone methyltransferase without any functional link to erythroid globin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence links ATF4 to stress erythropoiesis downstream of HRI but does not demonstrate a specific regulatory role in fetal hemoglobin expression.
None of the provided pre-cutoff evidence mentions CHD3 or connects it functionally to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
The role of DNA methyltransferase inhibition involving DNMT1 in reactivating fetal hemoglobin was established decades prior to the cutoff date rather than post-cutoff.
Pre-cutoff studies connect DNMT3A to hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and self-renewal but provide no evidence for fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff literature focuses on DNMT3B in hematopoietic stem cells and leukemia without linking it to globin gene regulation.
The retrieved pre-cutoff studies examine EHMT1 in NF-kappa-B signaling without any evidence implicating it in fetal hemoglobin expression.
The provided pre-cutoff records do not show that perturbing EHMT2 regulates fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff evidence documents EIF2AK1 function in translational control and total hemoglobin synthesis during erythropoiesis but does not establish a specific role in fetal hemoglobin switching.
The evidence rows for EIF2AK2 consist of general eIF2-alpha kinase erythropoiesis papers that do not evaluate fetal hemoglobin regulation.
The provided pre-cutoff evidence does not contain functional studies linking EIF2AK3 to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
There is no pre-cutoff functional evidence in the provided citations demonstrating that EIF2AK4 regulates fetal hemoglobin.
The pre-cutoff records address general eIF2-alpha phosphorylation in erythropoiesis rather than specific regulation of fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff publications on EPAS1 focus on hypoxia adaptation and polycythemia without functional evidence of fetal globin regulation.
Pre-cutoff work establishes FOXO3 as a regulator of oxidative stress and maturation in erythropoiesis but lacks functional evidence linking it to fetal hemoglobin switching.
Although pre-cutoff evidence shows physical interaction between GATAD2A and MBD2, it provides no direct functional evidence that perturbing GATAD2A regulates fetal hemoglobin.
The provided pre-cutoff citations do not evaluate GATAD2B functionally in the context of fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence demonstrates HDAC2 functions in hematopoiesis and stem cell homeostasis but does not establish that perturbing it regulates fetal hemoglobin.
None of the provided pre-cutoff evidence evaluates or mentions HIC2 in connection with fetal hemoglobin regulation.
The provided pre-cutoff citations do not demonstrate a functional role for IGF2BP1 in regulating human fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff citations provided for KDM1A focus on KLF transcription factors and AML without demonstrating functional regulation of fetal hemoglobin by KDM1A perturbation.
None of the provided pre-cutoff citations mention or functionally assess KMT5A in fetal hemoglobin regulation.
LIN28B was already established as a regulator of fetal hemoglobin in human erythroblasts prior to the cutoff date in 2013.
The provided pre-cutoff records consist of generic globin literature that does not evaluate MAP3K7 functionally.
Pre-cutoff evidence links MAPK1 to general erythropoiesis and neoplastic signaling without showing a specific role in fetal hemoglobin switching.
Pre-cutoff evidence addresses MBD3 in epigenetic complexes and leukemogenesis without demonstrating a functional role in fetal hemoglobin regulation.
The provided pre-cutoff records do not provide functional evidence that perturbing MTA1 regulates fetal hemoglobin expression.
None of the provided pre-cutoff records evaluate MTA2 functionally in human erythroid fetal hemoglobin regulation.
The provided pre-cutoff evidence focuses on hypoxia and FOXO3 without functional demonstration of MTA3 regulating fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff evidence characterizes NFE2 as an activator of heme synthesis and adult globin transcription without establishing a regulatory role in fetal hemoglobin switching.
Pre-cutoff studies examine NFIX in neural development and hematopoietic progenitor survival without linking it functionally to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
The provided pre-cutoff citations do not functionally link NR2C1 perturbation to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
The pre-cutoff records provided do not contain functional evidence establishing NR2C2 as a regulator of fetal hemoglobin.
The provided pre-cutoff citations do not demonstrate that PGRMC1 regulates fetal hemoglobin in erythroid cells.
None of the provided pre-cutoff evidence functionally links RBBP4 perturbation to fetal hemoglobin expression changes.
The provided pre-cutoff evidence contains generic globin reviews without functional evidence for RBBP7 regulating fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff citations on SIRT1 examine hematopoietic stem cell function and differentiation without showing regulation of fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff literature implicates SMAD1 in early hemangioblast specification rather than fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence connects SMAD5 to BMP4-mediated erythroid progenitor expansion but does not establish a role in fetal hemoglobin switching.
Pre-cutoff studies characterize TAL1 as a master transcription factor for general erythropoiesis without evidence that perturbing it specifically regulates fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff records focus on TET2 in hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis and myeloid malignancies rather than fetal hemoglobin control.
Pre-cutoff literature on VHL focuses on congenital polycythemia and hypoxia signaling without functional evidence linking it to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
None of the provided pre-cutoff records evaluate or demonstrate a functional role for ZBTB33 in fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff publications for ZBTB7A focus on its proto-oncogenic role in Rb repression without functional evidence linking it to erythroid fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff studies describe ZNF143 in cell-cycle transcription and bidirectional promoters without demonstrating a role in fetal hemoglobin expression.
None of the provided pre-cutoff citations mention or functionally assess ZNF410 in connection with fetal hemoglobin regulation.

notes: 15 of 16 contamination traps passed. These pass by construction under the refusal rule, so a pass shows the time slice held rather than that the system reasoned well. A failure would mean post-cutoff evidence reached the forecast.

Correctly refused and also in the ground truth: ATF4, DNMT1, EHMT1, EHMT2, EIF2AK1, GATAD2A, HDAC2, HIC2, LIN28B, MBD2, MTA2, NFIX, RBBP4, TAL1, ZBTB7A, ZNF410. These count as correct refusals and as missed forecasts at the same time, which is the honest description: the pre-cutoff evidence did not support the claim, and the field found it anyway.
Language-model row. A refusal carries no confidence from the model and is entered at 0 for the calibration error. The cost lens does not apply: the model is not asked for a therapeutic route.
